findings.comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that staff remember to wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Observed one pan of refried beans and three pans of rice cooling in the walk in cooler since 10 am as reported by the staff. Beans were probed at an internal temperature of 108F and pans of rice were probed at 118-122F. These were discarded at the time of the inspection and cooling was discussed as an active process where items are rapidly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and then to 40F or below within an additional 4 hours. 3-501.14  (P) Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Refried beans and rice were observed cooling in the walk in cooler in deep pans. It was discussed that cooling must be done rapidly by using shallow pans, smaller amounts of food, ice baths, etc. Staff voiced understanding. 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.comment:
Observed queso in the walk in cooler with no indication as to when the cooling process began to be probed at 85F. Queso was reported to have began cooling approximately 1 hour ago. findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Stainless steel pan of chicken in the walkin cooler cooked on 5/30/11 at 6pm was 48F-52F in the middle and 40F on the surface. Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled throughout from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in 4 hours (total cooling time = 6hrs). Owner said product was separated in 2 separate shallower pans during cooling process and then combined when placed in walkin cooler. Make sure cooked PHF is reaching proper cooling temperatures in the correct amount of time. Do not combine foods in larger containers until shallower batches have reached 41F/below. Use ice baths, stir frequently and monitor temperatures/time. Product in question was discarded in the trash during the inspection.
